metadata.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST

problem_summary.summary: Return the value at one-based position k in the BST's values when sorted in ascending order.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a BST root and integer k. Return the kth smallest node value.
constraints: 1 <= k <= n <= 10^4, where n is the number of nodes

brute_force.explanation: Use iterative inorder traversal to collect all values in sorted order, then return the value at index k - 1.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Inorder traversal of a BST lists its values in ascending order. Therefore the value stored at zero-based index k - 1 is exactly the one-based kth smallest value.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — the full inorder traversal visits every node.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for the collected values and traversal stack.

optimized.explanation: Traverse inorder iteratively but stop as soon as the kth node is popped from the stack.
optimized.correctness_idea: Nodes are popped in ascending order during inorder traversal. Counting these visits from one and returning at k therefore returns the kth smallest value, without visiting later nodes.
optimized.time_complexity: O(h + k) — descend to the leftmost node and visit through the kth inorder node; worst case is O(n).
optimized.space_complexity: O(h) auxiliary for the explicit traversal stack.

steps.event: Descend left from 8 through 4 to node 2.
steps.condition: Inorder traversal pushes ancestors before exploring their left children.
steps.action: Pop node 2 as the first value.

steps.condition: This is the second value in ascending order.
steps.action: Pop 4, then traverse its right child 6 before returning to 8.

steps.condition: After 6, the fourth popped node is 8, so visited equals k.

edge_cases.handling: The traversal returns the leftmost, smallest node.
The traversal reaches and returns the largest node.
An explicit stack avoids dependence on the Java call-stack depth.
